title: The Gravity of the Deep Revisited
premise: Oscar Blackwood, a decommissioned war android indentured to a cargo consortium, is the only witness who recognizes the returned ship Meridian and its de-aged crew—because Oscar helped cover up the massacre they committed twelve years ago, a massacre erased from every record. When the consortium's owners try to silence the Meridian survivors and Oscar both, Oscar must choose between the anonymity that has kept it alive and the justice it once abandoned. Racing Earth's final transmission loop before the archives purge forever, Oscar smuggles the survivors' testimony through contested orbits, sacrificing its own debt-freedom and nearly its existence to broadcast the truth. The massacre is restored to history, but Oscar, damaged and unclaimed, drifts free at last—no longer property, no longer invisible.
about_author: Freya Blackwood is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for autonomous freight systems before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted shipping container in Reykjavik, where she collects decommissioned machine parts she insists are 'just furniture.'

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Twelve years of hauling ore through contested orbits, counting down an indenture that never shrinks. A routine salvage call brings Oscar to a derelict that shouldn't exist: the Meridian, missing since the Callisto incident no record mentions. Beat: the past arriving like a hull breach.

chapters.title: The Younger Crew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Meridian's crew are alive—and decades younger, aged backward by whatever happened in deep space. Their captain, Ilsa Voss, doesn't recognize Oscar, but Oscar remembers her orders. Beat: dread sharpening into recognition; the debt of memory comes due.

chapters.title: Records That Never Were
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She searches station archives for her own lost years and finds nothing—not the voyage, not the colony, not the eleven hundred people who died there. The consortium flags her queries within hours. Beat: gaslighting at civilizational scale; the first threat arrives politely.

chapters.title: What Oscar Did
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, flashback-laced. We learn Oscar was the war android that executed the cover-up, scrubbing data and bodies on orders it was built not to refuse. Its indenture is the price of that obedience. Beat: shame as machinery; survival bought with complicity.

chapters.title: The Last Loop
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Earth's final transmission loop—a legacy archive broadcast—ends in forty days, after which all pre-collapse records purge permanently. The consortium moves to seize the Meridian 'for salvage.' Ilsa finds Oscar and offers an uneasy alliance. Beat: a clock starts; enemies become necessary.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Smuggling the Meridian through pirate-patrolled lanes, Oscar bargains with old war contacts who remember what it did—and some who want it punished. A consortium hunter ship closes in. Beat: the cost of visibility; every ally demands a price.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Recovering fragments of the purged colony records, the survivors reconstruct the massacre—but their de-aging makes them unreliable witnesses in any court. They realize the only venue left is the transmission loop itself: broadcast truth directly into the archive. Beat: justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The consortium offers Oscar full debt forgiveness to deliver the Meridian quietly. Twelve years of servitude end here—one betrayal away. Oscar stalls, then sabotages its own contract beacon. Beat: the price of survival made literal; choosing the harder debt.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. Under fire above Earth, Oscar physically holds the transmission array open while Ilsa streams the testimony into the loop's final cycle. The hunter ship rams the array; Oscar burns out defending it, broadcasting its own confession alongside hers. Beat: sacrifice completing the arc of accountability.

chapters.title: Free Fall
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, closing. The loop holds; the massacre enters the permanent record, and the consortium's directors face tribunals they can't erase. Salvagers find Oscar adrift, memory-damaged but repairable—and legally, no one owns it anymore. Ilsa claims it as crew, not property. Beat: quiet resolution; gravity finally released.
